questions.prompt: Use Trial 1 and Trial 2 to explain why Trial 1 detaches before the top while Trial 2 reaches the top at the ideal contact threshold. Use speed, gravity, normal force, and centripetal acceleration.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Trial 1 never has an on-track top speed; it detaches when the required normal force would become negative. Trial 2 reaches the top with N = 0 in the ideal model. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Accurately compares both trials and applies the inward-force condition. Partial credit: Correctly connects speed and contact but omits one force detail. No credit: Claims the track pulls the cart inward or treats Trial 1's hypothetical top speed as an observation.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion explaining how release height affects energy, speed, and contact in a vertical loop. Use numerical evidence from all three trials and distinguish conservation of energy from the centripetal-force requirement.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: A successful explanation must use both energy conservation and the top-of-loop force condition. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Gives a clear claim, cites accurate evidence from all three trials, explains PE-KE conversion, and correctly explains why sufficient energy alone does not replace the contact-force condition. Partial credit: Gives a supported energy explanation but incompletely treats contact. No credit: Claims energy is created or gives no trial evidence.
